standard_prerequisites.name: Signed tableau rules for negation
standard_prerequisites.statement: From the signed formula True (not A) the True-not rule derives False A; from False (not A) the False-not rule derives True A.
standard_prerequisites.use: The forward direction converts the witness tableau with the True-not rule; the reverse direction closes branches with the False-not rule.

standard_prerequisites.name: Inconsistency via closed tableaux
standard_prerequisites.statement: A finite signed assumption set is inconsistent iff it has a closed tableau.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both directions of the equivalence are phrased as existence of closed tableaux for the corresponding signed assumption sets.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 923-926): Gamma proves A iff Gamma union {not A} is inconsistent.

Forward direction (proof lines 928-940): given a closed tableau for {False A, True B_1,...,True B_n}, replace the first assumption by True (not A) and apply the True-not rule to obtain a closed tableau for {True (not A), True B_1,...,True B_n}.

Reverse direction (proof lines 942-955): remove every formula derived from the True (not A) assumption together with that assumption and add False A as an assumption; a branch that closed via the True-not conclusion False A stays closed, and a branch closed by the pair True (not A), False (not A) is closed by applying the False-not rule to False (not A), whose conclusion True A contradicts the added False A.
proof_roadmap: Convert the forward witness with one True-not application.
Reverse by deleting the not-A derivation and adding False A as an assumption.
Re-close every branch by case analysis on how it closed before.
difficulty_reason: Derivability-inconsistency equivalence (statement 923-926, proof 928-956): both directions carried in full, including the reverse branch-surgery case analysis. H2.
